claim: The Drosophila eye epithelium is patterned into a precise triangular grid of photoreceptor clusters called ommatidia.
source: Pattern formation of biological structures involves the arrangement of different types of cells in an ordered spatial configuration. In this study, we investigate the mechanism of patterning the Drosophila eye epithelium into a precise triangular grid of photoreceptor clusters called ommatidia.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as the subject of investigation.

claim: Previous studies proposed a reaction-diffusion process templated by recently formed ommatidia to propagate a molecular prepattern across the eye.
source: Previous studies had led to a long-standing biochemical model whereby a reaction-diffusion process is templated by recently formed ommatidia to propagate a molecular prepattern across the eye.
evidence: This claim references prior work and is supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: The templating mechanism for ommatidia patterning is mechanochemical in origin.
source: Here, we find that the templating mechanism is instead, mechanochemical in origin; newly born columns of differentiating ommatidia serve as a template to spatially pattern flows that move epithelial cells into position to form each new column of ommatidia.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: Cell flow is generated by a source and sink corresponding to narrow zones of cell dilation and contraction respectively.
source: Cell flow is generated by a source and sink, corresponding to narrow zones of cell dilation and contraction respectively, that straddle the growing wavefront of ommatidia.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data presented in the results.

claim: The newly formed lattice grid of ommatidia cells are immobile and deflect and focus the flow of other cells.
source: The newly formed lattice grid of ommatidia cells are immobile, deflecting, and focusing the flow of other cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by velocity measurements in the results.

claim: Grid cells of the mammalian cortex fire in a triangular grid pattern to encode a neural representation of Euclidean space.
source: For example, the grid cells of the mammalian cortex fire in a triangular grid pattern to encode a neural representation of Euclidean space (Rowland et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rowland et al., 2016.

claim: Photoreceptor cells of the insect compound eye fire in a triangular grid pattern to sense the visual environment with great acuity.
source: Likewise, the photoreceptor cells (R cells) of the insect compound eye fire in a triangular grid pattern to sense the visual environment with great acuity (Nilsson, 1989).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nilsson, 1989.

claim: Reaction-diffusion models posit that a molecular activator and inhibitor react with one another and effectively diffuse out from their sources of synthesis to generate a regular pattern of cell types.
source: A particular example of this class of models, the reaction-diffusion model, posits that a molecular activator and inhibitor react with one another and effectively diffuse out from their sources of synthesis, from which emerges a regular pattern of cell types (Meinhardt, 1982; Oster and Murray, 1989; Turing, 1952).
evidence: This claim describes a theoretical model and is supported by citations to foundational papers.

claim: Spaced patterns in living systems often progressively emerge in a directional manner, initializing at one region and then propagating across a tissue.
source: Similar to the engineering of crystals in industrial contexts, spaced patterns in living systems often progressively emerge in a directional manner, initializing at one region and then propagating across a tissue (Sato et al., 2013; Schweisguth and Corson, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Sato et al., 2013 and Schweisguth and Corson, 2019.

claim: The precise arrangement of follicles in the chick is impaired if the wavefront is decoupled from follicle self-organization.
source: Evidence to support this rationale comes from avian feather follicle development, where the precise arrangement of follicles in the chick is impaired if the wavefront is decoupled from follicle self-organization (Ho et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ho et al., 2019.

claim: Bird species that naturally lack a precise arrangement of feather primordia develop without a wavefront.
source: Bird species that naturally lack a precise arrangement of feather primordia develop without a wavefront (Ho et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ho et al., 2019.

claim: In the Drosophila retina, if two wavefronts are triggered then errors in R cell spacing occur.
source: In the Drosophila retina, if two wavefronts are triggered then errors in R cell spacing occur as a result (Heberlein et al., 1995; Ma and Moses, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Heberlein et al., 1995 and Ma and Moses, 1995.

claim: There is a wavefront of gene expression that initializes at the posterior edge of the epithelium and propagates across the field over a two-day period.
source: There is a wavefront of gene expression that initializes at the posterior edge of the epithelium and propagates across the field over a two-day period (Roignant and Treisman, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Roignant and Treisman, 2009.

claim: Cells were thought to remain motionless within the plane of the epithelium during eye development.
source: Cells are thought to remain motionless within the plane of the epithelium (Ready et al., 1976).
evidence: This claim describes a previous assumption and is supported by a citation to Ready et al., 1976.

claim: Atonal is a proneural transcription activator that is an essential member of the wave.
source: The gene atonal is an essential member of the wave, expressing a proneural transcription activator (Jarman et al., 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Jarman et al., 1994.

claim: Atonal activates expression of the scabrous gene.
source: Atonal activates expression of the scabrous gene (Jarman et al., 1994), which encodes a secreted glycoprotein (Baker et al., 1990; Lee et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jarman et al., 1994, Baker et al., 1990, and Lee et al., 1996.

claim: Scabrous encodes a secreted glycoprotein.
source: Atonal activates expression of the scabrous gene (Jarman et al., 1994), which encodes a secreted glycoprotein (Baker et al., 1990; Lee et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Baker et al., 1990 and Lee et al., 1996.

claim: Loss of Scabrous results in ommatidia that are spaced too close to one another and exhibit loss of regularity.
source: Loss of Scabrous results in ommatidia that are spaced too close to one another and exhibit loss of regularity (Baker et al., 1990; Wolff and Ready, 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Baker et al., 1990 and Wolff and Ready, 1991.

claim: Atonal expression becomes crowded and irregular in scabrous mutants.
source: Atonal expression also becomes crowded and irregular in scabrous mutants (Lee et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 1996.

claim: Reaction-diffusion models have proposed Scabrous as a long-range inhibitor of the activator Atonal.
source: Reaction-diffusion models have proposed Scabrous as a long-range inhibitor of the activator Atonal, and such models successfully simulate the sequential emergence of ordered ommatidia in a tissue of stationary cells (Lubensky et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lubensky et al., 2011.

claim: The wavefront of gene expression is coincident with a physical deformation of the epithelium brought about by a constriction of cells' apical domains to form a dorsal-ventral furrow called the morphogenetic furrow.
source: The wavefront of gene expression is coincident with a physical deformation of the epithelium brought about by a constriction of cells' apical domains to form a dorsal-ventral furrow called the morphogenetic furrow (MF) (Wolff and Ready, 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wolff and Ready, 1991.

claim: As the wave passes, most cells expand their apical domains on the posterior side except for the clusters of nascent R cells, which remain apically constricted.
source: As the wave passes, most cells expand their apical domains on the posterior side except for the clusters of nascent R cells, which remain apically constricted.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is supported by prior literature.

claim: The wave of gene expression is coupled to a mechanical wave.
source: Thus, the wave of gene expression is coupled to a mechanical wave (Brown et al., 2006; Escudero et al., 2007; Wolff and Ready, 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brown et al., 2006, Escudero et al., 2007, and Wolff and Ready, 1991.

claim: Myosin-induced apical constriction in the furrow is regulated by the signals that also regulate atonal expression.
source: Reaction-diffusion models successfully mimic pattern formation in vivo without any obligatory cell shape or cell flow dynamics (Gavish et al., 2016; Lubensky et al., 2011), and myosin-induced apical constriction in the furrow is regulated by the signals that also regulate atonal expression (Escudero et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Escudero et al., 2007.

claim: Approximately 36 hr before pupariation, the mechanochemical wave begins to move across the eye disc from the posterior edge.
source: Approximately 36 hr before pupariation, the mechanochemical wave begins to move across the eye disc from the posterior edge (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Over the course of 2 days, the MF crosses the disc.
source: Over the course of 2 days, the MF crosses the disc (Ready et al., 1976).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ready et al., 1976.

claim: As the MF migrates to the anterior, a column of regularly spaced ommatidia emerge every two hours.
source: As it migrates to the anterior, a column of regularly spaced ommatidia emerge every two hours (Wolff and Ready, 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wolff and Ready, 1991.

claim: Each emergent ommatidium is composed of five cells that are destined to become R2, R3, R4, R5, and R8 photoreceptors.
source: Each emergent ommatidium is composed of five cells that are destined to become R2, R3, R4, R5, and R8 photoreceptors (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Cells within an ommatidium remain apically constricted and form a rosette structure while non-ommatidia cells are structurally disordered.
source: Cells within an ommatidium remain apically constricted and form a rosette structure while non-ommatidia cells are structurally disordered (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Each ommatidium recruits cells to become R1, R6, and R7, whose apical faces undergo constriction.
source: Subsequently, each ommatidium recruits cells to become R1, R6, and R7, whose apical faces undergo constriction.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The regular spacing of ommatidia between two adjacent columns is out of phase such that a regular triangular grid, with odd and even columns of ommatidia, is generated in the domain posterior to the MF.
source: The regular spacing of ommatidia between two adjacent columns is out of phase such that a regular triangular grid, with odd and even columns of ommatidia, is generated in the domain posterior to the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Disc explants routinely sustained development for 10–12 hr.
source: Disc explants routinely sustained development for 10–12 hr, which enabled us to capture a rich set of developmental events from a single sample.
evidence: This is stated in the results section describing the experimental method.

claim: The MF progressed from posterior to anterior, and a new column of ommatidia appeared at intervals of 2.0–2.5 hr.
source: The MF progressed from posterior to anterior, and a new column of ommatidia appeared at intervals of 2.0–2.5 hr (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The rate of MF movement ex vivo is in accordance with the estimated interval of two hours per column for in vivo development.
source: This rate of MF movement is in accordance with the estimated interval of two hours per column for in vivo development (Campos-Ortega and Hofbauer, 1977).
evidence: This claim compares ex vivo observations to in vivo estimates and is supported by a citation to Campos-Ortega and Hofbauer, 1977.

claim: Over the course of a typical imaging session, 4–5 columns of ommatidia emerged.
source: Over the course of a typical imaging session, we were thus able to observe the emergence of 4–5 columns of ommatidia.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The spacing of ommatidia in adjacent columns exhibited an alternating phase such that a triangular grid pattern of ommatidia emerged from the cultured eye discs.
source: The spacing of ommatidia in adjacent columns exhibited an alternating phase such that a triangular grid pattern of ommatidia emerged from the cultured eye discs (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: A line of adjacent cells at the posterior edge of the MF progressively bent to form multicellular arcs containing 10–15 cells.
source: A line of adjacent cells at the posterior edge of the MF progressively bent to form multicellular arcs containing 10–15 cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Multicellular arcs evolved into immature rosettes of variable cell number, containing six to nine cells.
source: These arcs evolved into immature rosettes of variable cell number, containing six to nine cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The transition from arcs to immature rosettes was driven by a series of intercalations that brought cells together in the dorsal-ventral direction and displaced cells to the anterior.
source: This transition was driven by a series of intercalations that brought cells together in the dorsal-ventral direction and displaced cells to the anterior (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The cell fated to become R8 was typically at the most posterior position of the immature rosette.
source: We observed that the cell fated to become R8 was typically at the most posterior position of the immature rosette (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: The immature rosette evolved into a five-cell mature rosette, containing cells fated to differentiate into R2, R3, R4, R5, and R8.
source: The immature rosette evolved into a five-cell mature rosette, containing cells fated to differentiate into R2, R3, R4, R5, and R8.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: One to three cells in the immature rosette, called mystery cells, relaxed their apical domains and were ejected from the rosette.
source: One to three cells in the immature rosette, called mystery cells in prior studies (Tomlinson and Ready, 1987; Wolff and Ready, 1991), relaxed their apical domains and were ejected from the rosette (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in figures, with citations to prior studies.

claim: After establishment of the mature rosette, recruitment of the other three photoreceptor types, R1, R6, and R7, as well as the recruitment of the non-neuronal cone cells was observed.
source: After establishment of the mature rosette, we observed recruitment of the other three photoreceptor types, R1, R6, and R7, as well as the recruitment of the non-neuronal cone cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The trajectory of observed ommatidium development was highly reproducible between different eye discs.
source: The trajectory of observed ommatidium development was highly reproducible between different eye discs (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C) and entirely consistent with the trajectory inferred from fixed tissue experiments (Escudero et al., 2007; Tomlinson and Ready, 1987; Wolff and Ready, 1991).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, with citations to prior studies.

claim: Cell division was detected by the rounding up of cells on the adherens junction plane prior to cytokinesis, after which two daughter cells were observed.
source: Cell division was detected by the rounding up of cells on the adherens junction plane prior to cytokinesis, after which two daughter cells were observed (Figure 1G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: There was a zone of proliferation 10–20 μm anterior to the MF that abruptly ended at the anterior edge of MF.
source: There was a zone of proliferation 10–20 μm anterior to the MF that abruptly ended at the anterior edge of MF.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: No cell division was detected in the MF and in a narrow region ~7 μm to its posterior.
source: No cell division was detected in the MF and in a narrow region ~7 μm to its posterior.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: After the non-proliferative zone, cells resumed proliferation but it was limited to a narrow zone of cells, and little proliferation was observed in more posterior regions.
source: After this point, cells resumed proliferation but it was limited to a narrow zone of cells, and little proliferation was observed in more posterior regions.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Proliferation in the posterior zone was restricted to non-ommatidial cells, whereas cells in ommatidia remained non-proliferative.
source: Proliferation in this zone was restricted to non-ommatidial cells, whereas cells in ommatidia remained non-proliferative (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1H.

claim: The complex pattern of proliferation observed mimics the in vivo cell division pattern.
source: The complex pattern of proliferation we reproducibly observed mimics the in vivo cell division pattern (Ready et al., 1976; Wolff and Ready, 1991).
evidence: This claim compares ex vivo observations to in vivo patterns and is supported by citations to Ready et al., 1976 and Wolff and Ready, 1991.

claim: Ommatidia in the fourth column posterior to the MF began to rotate relative to their cell neighbors.
source: Ommatidia in the fourth column posterior to the MF began to rotate relative to their cell neighbors (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1I.

claim: Clusters rotated 90° and rotation was either clockwise or counterclockwise depending on which side of the equator the clusters were located.
source: Clusters rotated 90° and rotation was either clockwise or counterclockwise depending on which side of the equator (i.e. dorsal-ventral midline) the clusters were located.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Full rotation occurred in two steps of 45° each.
source: We observed that full rotation occurred in two steps of 45° each (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Upregulated expression of E-cadherin protein was observed in all cells within the MF, within the emerging rosettes, and within maturing ommatidia.
source: Finally, we observed upregulated expression of E-cadherin protein in all cells within the MF, within the emerging rosettes, and within maturing ommatidia (Figure 1I and J).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 1I and J.

claim: E-cadherin upregulation was previously observed and attributed to transcriptional activation of the E-cadherin gene by Atonal, and post-transcriptional activation of the gene by the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor.
source: This upregulation was previously observed and attributed to transcriptional activation of the E-cadherin gene by Atonal, and post-transcriptional activation of the gene by the Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) (Brown et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brown et al., 2006.

claim: Cultured eye discs exhibited features of development that eye discs in vivo have been inferred to have.
source: In conclusion, the cultured eye discs exhibited features of development that eye discs in vivo have been inferred to have. This gives us confidence that our system is an accurate model of in vivo eye patterning.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the results section based on comparisons to prior literature.

claim: Previous studies had inferred that cells in the eye disc do not significantly migrate or move with respect to one another.
source: Previous studies had inferred that cells in the eye disc do not significantly migrate or move with respect to one another (Campos-Ortega and Hofbauer, 1977; Ready et al., 1976).
evidence: This claim describes a previous assumption and is supported by citations to Campos-Ortega and Hofbauer, 1977 and Ready et al., 1976.

claim: An unexpected collective cell flow pattern in the MF directed toward the anterior was observed.
source: We investigated the accuracy of this assumption by tracking individual cells within the MF and estimating the velocity of each cell over time. We observed an unexpected collective cell flow pattern in the MF directed toward the anterior (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Cells were observed to collectively flow together within clusters of 15–25 cells.
source: Cells were observed to collectively flow together within clusters of 15–25 cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Clusters flowed at a similar anterior velocity as other clusters, forming a periodic pattern of flow along the dorsal-ventral axis.
source: Clusters flowed at a similar anterior velocity as other clusters, forming a periodic pattern of flow along the dorsal-ventral axis.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The clusters with high anterior flow were moving at a similar velocity (1.2–1.5 μm/hr) to the MF, which moved at 1.44 μm/hr.
source: The clusters with high anterior flow were moving at a similar velocity (1.2–1.5 μm/hr) to the MF, which moved at 1.44 μm/hr (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Clusters with lower flow moved at 0.35–0.55 μm/hr.
source: Clusters with lower flow moved at 0.35–0.55 μm/hr.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The periodic flow field was stable throughout the time course of imaging and was localized to the MF.
source: This periodic flow field was stable throughout the time course of imaging and was localized to the MF (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The period length of the flow field matched the average distance between neighboring ommatidia within the same column posterior to the MF.
source: Strikingly, the period length of the flow field matched the average distance between neighboring ommatidia within the same column posterior to the MF (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: A cluster at a fixed position along the dorsal-ventral axis that experienced high flow would then experience low flow approximately 2 hr later, and vice versa.
source: A cluster at a fixed position along the dorsal-ventral axis that experienced high flow would then experience low flow approximately 2 hr later, and vice versa (Figure 2A and D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 2A and D.

claim: All clusters oscillated in the magnitude of their flow over time with a regular period length of ~4 hr.
source: Thus, all clusters oscillated in the magnitude of their flow over time with a regular period length of ~4 hr (Figure 2E), the same time taken to form two new columns of ommatidia.
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: Periodic fluctuations in velocity were synchronized between cells in the MF that were added to columns of the same parity.
source: Periodic fluctuations in velocity were synchronized between cells in the MF that were added to columns of the same parity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Velocity fluctuations were out of phase to the velocity field that occurred in cells being added to columns of the opposite parity.
source: These fluctuations were out of phase to the velocity field that occurred in cells being added to columns of the opposite parity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Each group of presumptive R cells moved to the anterior at a constant speed, but then abruptly stopped moving.
source: Each group of presumptive R cells moved to the anterior at a constant speed, but then abruptly stopped moving.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: At the inflection point, the group of five presumptive R cells were arranged in a linear configuration within the MF.
source: At this inflection point, the group of five presumptive R cells were arranged in a linear configuration within the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Approximately two hours after presumptive R cells stopped moving, they had formed arcs and were clearly exiting the MF.
source: Approximately two hours after they stopped moving, they had formed arcs and were clearly exiting the MF (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Presumptive R cells fated to form different columns moved at similar speeds to one another but stopped moving at phase-varied 2-hr intervals.
source: Presumptive R cells fated to form different columns moved at similar speeds to one another but stopped moving at phase-varied 2-hr intervals.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Clusters of cells experiencing high anterior flow contained presumptive R8 cells that had comparable anterior velocities.
source: Clusters of cells experiencing high anterior flow contained presumptive R8 cells that had comparable anterior velocities, suggesting that R cells were flowing coherently with the fast-moving clusters (Figure 3C and D, Table 1 and Video 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3C and D, Table 1, and Video 3.

claim: Clusters with lower flow contained presumptive R8 cells with divergent velocity behaviors.
source: In contrast, clusters with lower flow contained presumptive R8 cells with divergent velocity behaviors (Figure 3C and E, Table 1 and Video 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 3C and E, Table 1, and Video 3.

claim: Presumptive R8s on the anterior side of the MF were flowing coherently with the slow-moving clusters.
source: Presumptive R8s on the anterior side of the MF were flowing coherently with the slow-moving clusters.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Presumptive R8s on the posterior side of the MF had stopped moving or were moving in a posterior direction.
source: However, presumptive R8s on the posterior side of the MF had stopped moving or were moving in a posterior direction.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: All presumptive R8s in both high-flow and low-flow clusters within the MF exhibited a clearly bimodal behavior in their anterior velocity.
source: When we considered all presumptive R8s in both high-flow and low-flow clusters within the MF, a clearly bimodal behavior in their anterior velocity was observed, and this was a stable property of the MF over the time course of imaging (Figure 3F, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3F and Table 1.

claim: Cells located immediately anterior to the MF primarily flowed in an anterior direction but without periodicity.
source: Cells located immediately anterior to the MF primarily flowed in an anterior direction but without periodicity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: A narrow zone of cells anterior to the MF had little or no anterior-posterior movement on average.
source: This zone was positioned beside a narrow zone of cells that, on average, had little or no anterior-posterior movement, and anterior to that zone, cells appeared to be primarily moving in a posterior direction.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Cells immediately posterior to the MF flowed in an anterior direction.
source: Immediately posterior to the MF, cells flowed in an anterior direction.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Further posterior to the MF was a narrow zone of cells that, on average, had little or no anterior-posterior movement.
source: Further posterior was a narrow zone of cells that, on average, had little or no anterior-posterior movement, and posterior to that zone, all cells were moving in a posterior direction.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: These patterns of cell flow were a stable feature of the eye disc over the time course of imaging.
source: These patterns of cell flow were a stable feature of the eye disc over the time course of imaging (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Periodic cell flows contribute to the emergence of regularly spaced ommatidia.
source: In sum, these observations led us to hypothesize that periodic cell flows contribute to the emergence of regularly spaced ommatidia.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the results section based on the data.

claim: Reduced flow on the posterior side of the MF leads to groups of cells leaving the MF by virtue of having stopped moving at the same velocity as the furrow.
source: Reduced flow on the posterior side of the MF leads to groups of cells leaving the MF by virtue of having stopped moving at the same velocity as the furrow.
evidence: This is part of the hypothesis stated in the results section.

claim: A subset of cells in each group that leaves the MF then form an ommatidium.
source: A subset of cells in each group then form an ommatidium.
evidence: This is part of the hypothesis stated in the results section.

claim: The periodic flow ensures that the groups of cells leaving the MF at any given point in time are regularly spaced apart.
source: Since the flow is periodic, it ensures that the groups of cells leaving the MF at any given point in time are regularly spaced apart.
evidence: This is part of the hypothesis stated in the results section.

claim: The alternating phase of periodic flow in the MF over time ensures that groups of cells at the same dorsal-ventral position leave the MF every 4–5 hr or in every second column.
source: Moreover, the alternating phase of periodic flow in the MF over time ensures that groups of cells at the same dorsal-ventral position leave the MF every 4–5 hr or in every second column, thus generating a triangular grid pattern that is coherent with the already patterned portion of the lattice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Video 4).
evidence: This is part of the hypothesis stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1 and Video 4.

claim: The atonal gene is initially expressed uniformly in a dorsal-ventral stripe of cells in the MF that is resolved posteriorly into evenly spaced clusters of cells of decreasing number until atonal is expressed exclusively in presumptive R8 cells.
source: The atonal gene is initially expressed uniformly in a dorsal-ventral stripe of cells in the MF that is resolved posteriorly into evenly spaced clusters of cells of decreasing number until atonal is expressed exclusively in presumptive R8 cells (Frankfort and Mardon, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Frankfort and Mardon, 2002.

claim: The Atonal proneural transcription factor triggers a program of gene expression leading to R8 specification.
source: The Atonal proneural transcription factor then triggers a program of gene expression leading to R8 specification (Pepple et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pepple et al., 2008.

claim: Transcription of E-cadherin is strongly activated by Atonal in R cells as they exit the MF, while non-R cells downregulate E-cadherin transcription.
source: Transcription of E-cadherin is strongly activated by Atonal in R cells as they exit the MF, while non-R cells downregulate E-cadherin transcription (Brown et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brown et al., 2006.

claim: Loss of atonal expression results in no upregulation of E-cadherin transcription in R cells.
source: Loss of atonal expression results in no upregulation of E-cadherin transcription in R cells (Brown et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brown et al., 2006.

claim: All cells within the MF expressed equivalent levels of E-cadherin.
source: All cells within the MF expressed equivalent levels of E-cadherin (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: When cells exited the MF, a bifurcation in E-cadherin expression dynamics appeared.
source: When cells exited the MF, a bifurcation in E-cadherin expression dynamics appeared.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Some cells progressively increased E-cadherin expression over time while other cells reduced their expression after exiting the MF.
source: Some cells progressively increased E-cadherin expression over time while other cells reduced their expression.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The cells classified as being R cells based on apical shape and position were exclusively those that increased E-cadherin expression.
source: The cells we had classified as being R cells based on apical shape and position were exclusively those that increased E-cadherin expression (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 3H.

claim: The mechanical process observed was generating a lattice pattern of proneural gene expression.
source: Thus, the mechanical process we were observing was generating a lattice pattern of proneural gene expression.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the E-cadherin expression data.

claim: Any perturbation that disrupts the periodic cell flow would generate irregular spacing of ommatidia.
source: An important prediction of our hypothesis is that any perturbation that disrupts the periodic cell flow would generate irregular spacing of ommatidia.
evidence: This is a prediction stated in the results section.

claim: Scabrous is a secreted glycoprotein that is required for regular spacing of ommatidia.
source: Scabrous is a secreted glycoprotein that is required for regular spacing of ommatidia, and its loss results in irregular crowding of ommatidia (Baker et al., 1990; Lee et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Baker et al., 1990 and Lee et al., 1996.

claim: Cell division and delamination in scabrous mutant discs were comparable to wildtype.
source: Cell division and delamination were comparable to wildtype, and the MF transited at a velocity comparable to wildtype (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The MF in scabrous mutant discs transited at a velocity comparable to wildtype.
source: Cell division and delamination were comparable to wildtype, and the MF transited at a velocity comparable to wildtype (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Different scabrous mutant discs had spacing defects that ranged from mild to severe.
source: We found different mutant discs had spacing defects that ranged from mild to severe, as had been previously reported with fixed samples.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Discs with strong scabrous defects showed an abnormally large number of ommatidia emerge from the MF to form each column.
source: Discs with strong defects showed an abnormally large number of ommatidia emerge from the MF to form each column (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Ommatidia clusters in strong scabrous mutants did not emerge with regular spacing, and frequently two neighboring clusters appeared to fuse together as they emerged.
source: Ommatidia clusters did not emerge with regular spacing, and frequently two neighboring clusters appeared to fuse together as they emerged.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Scabrous mutant discs with strong spacing defects displayed a major impairment in flow within the MF.
source: The scabrous mutant discs with strong spacing defects displayed a major impairment in flow within the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: There was an almost complete absence of the periodicity in cell flow in strong scabrous mutants that had been observed in wildtype.
source: There was an almost complete absence of the periodicity in cell flow that had been observed in wildtype (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: There were no discernible clusters of cells with similar anterior velocity in strong scabrous mutants.
source: There were no discernible clusters of cells with similar anterior velocity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Cells all along the dorsal-ventral axis of the MF in strong scabrous mutants exhibited more uniform velocities.
source: Rather, cells all along the dorsal-ventral axis of the MF exhibited more uniform velocities (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Non-R cells in the MF of strong scabrous mutants had comparable velocity to the average velocity observed within wildtype clusters having lower flow.
source: When we compared the velocities of non-R cells in the MF between mutant and wildtype, mutant cells had comparable velocity to the average velocity observed within wildtype clusters having lower flow (Figure 4D').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4D'.

claim: Presumptive R8 cells in strong scabrous mutants displayed a loss of the wildtype bimodality in R8 velocity and uniformly resembled the wildtype R8s with low velocity.
source: A similar observation was made for the presumptive R8 cells; mutant cells displayed a loss of the wildtype bimodality in R8 velocity and uniformly resembled the wildtype R8s with low velocity (Figure 4D'').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4D''.

claim: Scabrous mutant discs with mild spacing defects had an irregular triangular lattice structure due to occasionally misplaced ommatidia emerging from the MF.
source: We also analyzed scabrousBP2 mutant discs with mild spacing defects. These had an irregular triangular lattice structure due to occasionally misplaced ommatidia emerging from the MF (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Scabrous mutant discs with mild defects had a correspondingly milder impairment in the periodicity of cell flows in the MF.
source: These discs had a correspondingly milder impairment in the periodicity of cell flows in the MF (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 4F and G.

claim: Cells on the posterior side of the MF in weak scabrous mutants had a diminished flow compared to wildtype.
source: Cells on the posterior side of the MF had a diminished flow compared to wildtype (Figure 4H and H').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 4H and H'.

claim: Presumptive R8 cells in weak scabrous mutants displayed bimodality in their velocity as with wildtype, but the magnitude of velocity overall was reduced.
source: Although presumptive R8 cells displayed bimodality in their velocity as with wildtype, the magnitude of velocity overall was reduced (Figure 4H'').
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 4H''.

claim: Scabrous not only perturbs both spacing and flow but it does so comparably for both phenomena.
source: Thus, scabrous not only perturbs both spacing and flow but it does so comparably for both phenomena.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the scabrous mutant data.

claim: Scabrous regulates ommatidia spacing by inducing periodic clusters of cells in the MF to flow with it before slowing down to form a new column.
source: We therefore posit that Scabrous regulates ommatidia spacing by inducing periodic clusters of cells in the MF to flow with it before slowing down to form a new column.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section.

claim: The Scabrous protein is exclusively synthesized in R cells as they emerge from the MF, and protein expression is maintained in R8 cells within the first three columns.
source: The Scabrous protein is exclusively synthesized in R cells as they emerge from the MF, and protein expression is maintained in R8 cells within the first three columns (Mlodzik et al., 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Mlodzik et al., 1990.

claim: Experiments with genetically mosaic eyes indicate that Scabrous acts non cell-autonomously and must be expressed in R8 cells for normal patterning.
source: Experiments with genetically mosaic eyes indicate that Scabrous acts non cell-autonomously and must be expressed in R8 cells for normal patterning (Baker et al., 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Baker et al., 1990.

claim: Newly formed ommatidia act as a chemical template to regulate strong periodic cell flows in an anterior direction within the MF in a manner dependent on Scabrous.
source: Thus, newly formed ommatidia act as a chemical template to regulate strong periodic cell flows in an anterior direction within the MF in a manner dependent on Scabrous.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section.

claim: Oriented rearrangements of cell shape and cell neighbors within the MF did not exhibit strong signatures of periodicity.
source: Oriented rearrangements of cell shape and cell neighbors within the MF did not exhibit strong signatures of periodicity, and in fact cells within the MF showed few such rearrangements (Videos 6 and 7).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Videos 6 and 7.

claim: Large-scale cellular contraction and dilation events were observed occurring on the anterior and posterior sides of the MF, respectively.
source: However, we observed large-scale cellular contraction and dilation events occurring on the anterior and posterior sides of the MF, respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The rate of cell contraction was maximal in a narrow zone of cells located ~10 μm anterior to the MF.
source: This one-dimensional perspective of the rate of change of apical area clearly showed that the rate of cell contraction was maximal in a narrow zone of cells located ~10 μm anterior to the MF, while the rate of dilation was maximal in cells located ~10 μm posterior (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The rate of dilation was maximal in cells located ~10 μm posterior to the MF.
source: This one-dimensional perspective of the rate of change of apical area clearly showed that the rate of cell contraction was maximal in a narrow zone of cells located ~10 μm anterior to the MF, while the rate of dilation was maximal in cells located ~10 μm posterior (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Cells in the anterior and posterior zones of maximal contraction and dilation were on average not flowing in either an anterior or posterior direction.
source: Cells in these two zones corresponded to cells that we had previously observed were on average not flowing in either an anterior or posterior direction (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5C.

claim: On either side of the anterior zone of contractility, cells flowed toward the zone.
source: On either side of the anterior zone of contractility, cells flowed toward the zone, while on either side of the posterior zone of dilation, cells flowed away from the zone.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: On either side of the posterior zone of dilation, cells flowed away from the zone.
source: On either side of the anterior zone of contractility, cells flowed toward the zone, while on either side of the posterior zone of dilation, cells flowed away from the zone.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: These trends are consistent with pressure gradients originating along bands of cells anterior and posterior to the MF, leading to the complex cell flows observed in the eye disc.
source: These trends are consistent with pressure gradients originating along bands of cells anterior and posterior to the MF, leading to the complex cell flows observed in the eye disc.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the results section.

claim: In scabrous mutants, cells posterior to the MF dilated to an average size that was 25–33% lower than in wildtype.
source: In scabrous mutants, cells posterior to the MF dilated to an average size that was 25–33% lower than in wildtype (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The reduced cell size in scabrous mutants was due to a marked reduction in the rate of dilation for scabrous mutant cells posterior to the MF.
source: This was due to a marked reduction in the rate of dilation for scabrous mutant cells posterior to the MF (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: The maximal rate of dilation in scabrous mutants was reduced by 75% and occurred closer to the MF than wildtype.
source: The maximal rate of dilation was reduced by 75% and occurred closer to the MF than wildtype.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Cell contraction dynamics anterior to the MF in scabrous mutants were identical to wildtype.
source: In contrast, cell contraction dynamics anterior to the MF were identical to wildtype (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In scabrous mutant discs, reduced anterior flow on the anterior side of the posterior dilation zone and reduced posterior flow on the posterior side were observed.
source: We hypothesized that if cell dilation in the posterior zone is generating pressure gradients, then in scabrous mutant discs, we would observe reduced anterior flow on the anterior side of the zone and reduced posterior flow on the posterior side. This expectation was confirmed in the mutant discs (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The rate of velocity change of cells away from the posterior zone in scabrous mutants was diminished, consistent with an abatement in the forces generating flow.
source: As well, the rate of velocity change of cells away from the posterior zone was also diminished, consistent with an abatement in the forces generating flow (Figure 5G).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 5G.

claim: The inflection point of cell flow in scabrous mutant discs was shifted closer to the MF, consistent with the anterior shift in the zone of maximal dilation rate.
source: Finally, the inflection point of cell flow in scabrous mutant discs was shifted closer to the MF, consistent with the anterior shift in the zone of maximal dilation rate (Figure 5E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figures 5E and F.

claim: The correlations between different features in the scabrous mutant discs lend support to the hypothesis that the posterior dilation zone generates a pressure gradient leading to cell flows.
source: These correlations between different features in the mutant discs lend further support to the hypothesis that the posterior dilation zone generates a pressure gradient leading to cell flows.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section.

claim: Only the anterior side of the posterior dilation zone exhibited strong bimodality in velocity.
source: If there was an intrinsically periodic pressure gradient, we would observe a bimodal distribution of velocities on the posterior side as well as on the anterior side. This was not observed; only the anterior side exhibited strong bimodality in velocity (Figure 6B, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6B and Table 1.

claim: A periodic flow profile can be generated by a uniform pressure gradient and a periodicity in the location of boundaries.
source: Pressure gradients in viscous fluids generate flow fields. The emergent flow profile generated, however, must accommodate boundaries, suggesting that a periodic flow profile can be generated by a uniform pressure gradient and a periodicity in the location of boundaries.
evidence: This is a theoretical consideration stated in the results section.

claim: Ommatidia in the act of formation become immobile within the flow field anterior to the dilation zone, forming a periodic array of rigid boundaries.
source: We considered a mechanism whereby ommatidia in the act of formation become immobile within the flow field anterior to the dilation zone, forming a periodic array of rigid boundaries. (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the results and shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Rigid boundaries formed by immobile ommatidia could deflect and focus the flow around them generating periodicity in the flow.
source: These rigid boundaries could deflect and focus the flow around them generating periodicity in the flow.
evidence: This is part of the hypothesis stated in the results section.

claim: Presumptive R8 cells rapidly decreased their velocity as they emerged from the MF and they stopped moving when they were positioned several μm anterior to the position where all other cells also stopped moving.
source: The presumptive R8 cells rapidly decreased their velocity as they emerged from the MF and they stopped moving when they were positioned several μm anterior to the position where all other cells also stopped moving.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The other R cells in each rosette also slowed down far earlier than non-ommatidial cells.
source: The other R cells in each rosette also slowed down far earlier than non-ommatidial cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: As ommatidia matured to become members of the third column, they reached the zone where all cells stopped moving.
source: As ommatidia matured to become members of the third column, they reached the zone where all cells stopped moving (also the zone of maximum dilation).
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: At the zone of maximum dilation, all of the R cells and non-ommatidial cells began to flow in the posterior direction at the same velocity.
source: There, all of the R cells and non-ommatidial cells began to flow in the posterior direction at the same velocity (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Ommatidia in the first three columns are immobile relative to the non-R cell flow field.
source: Thus, ommatidia in the first three columns are immobile relative to the non-R cell flow field.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section.

claim: Velocity profiles of maturing R cells in scabrous mutant discs were highly similar to wildtype.
source: We measured velocity profiles of maturing R cells in scabrous mutant discs and found them to be highly similar to wildtype (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Scabrous expression in R8 cells is not responsible for the transient immobility of ommatidia.
source: Therefore, Scabrous expression in R8 cells is not responsible for the transient immobility of ommatidia.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the scabrous mutant data.

claim: There is a source and sink of cell flow that straddles the MF.
source: In summary, we have described a complex set of phenomena never before observed in development of the Drosophila eye (Figure 7A). There is a source and sink of cell flow that straddles the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The source and sink are narrow stripes of cells oriented parallel to the MF and located at fixed distances from the MF.
source: The source and sink are narrow stripes of cells oriented parallel to the MF and located at fixed distances from the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The source and sink generate complex cell flows across the eye disc, including periodic flow in the MF.
source: They generate complex cell flows across the eye disc, including periodic flow in the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: As ommatidia emerge from the MF, they are initially immobile and do not flow with their non-R cell neighbors.
source: As ommatidia emerge from the MF, they are initially immobile and do not flow with their non-R cell neighbors.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: When the immobile ommatidia reach the flow source posterior to the MF, they abruptly become mobile and begin to flow with surrounding cells.
source: When the immobile ommatidia reach the flow source posterior to the MF, they abruptly become mobile and begin to flow with surrounding cells.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The observations strongly argue against the long-standing model for ommatidia patterning, which invoked local cell-cell interactions directly regulating the R cell gene expression program to create a lattice prepattern in the wake of the MF.
source: These observations strongly argue against the long-standing model for ommatidia patterning, which invoked local cell-cell interactions directly regulating the R cell gene expression program to create a lattice prepattern in the wake of the MF (reviewed in Frankfort and Mardon, 2002; Roignant and Treisman, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with citations to review articles.

claim: The prior model relied upon all cells remaining immobile with respect to one another as the MF passes.
source: That model relied upon all cells remaining immobile with respect to one another as the MF passes, so that long-range lateral inhibitors emanating from newly formed ommatidia would establish stable zones of non-neural fate (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Cells within the MF significantly move with respect to one another, a condition that precludes a standard reaction-diffusion mechanism from creating a regular prepattern of gene expression.
source: Instead, we have found that cells within the MF significantly move with respect to one another, a condition that precludes a standard reaction-diffusion mechanism from creating a regular prepattern of gene expression.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Groups of cells within the MF flow at the same velocity as the MF, and they alternate with groups of cells flowing at a much lower velocity.
source: Groups of cells within the MF flow at the same velocity as the MF, and they alternate with groups of cells flowing at a much lower velocity.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Groups of cells flowing at lower velocity are left behind on the posterior side of the MF and form a new column of ommatidia.
source: These latter groups are left behind on the posterior side of the MF and form a new column of ommatidia.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Flow in the MF is generated by the source and sink that straddle the MF.
source: Flow in the MF is generated by the source and sink that straddle the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The posterior source of cell flow precisely corresponds to a zone of cell dilation.
source: The posterior source of cell flow precisely corresponds to a zone of cell dilation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The dilation zone creates a pressure gradient, which causes cells in the MF to flow away from the source.
source: We suggest the dilation zone creates a pressure gradient, which causes cells in the MF to flow away from the source (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The anterior sink of cell flow precisely corresponds to a zone of cell contraction.
source: The anterior sink of cell flow precisely corresponds to a zone of cell contraction, suggesting that it contributes to the pressure gradient and augments cell flow in the MF towards the sink (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Flow in the MF is non-uniform owing to the lattice grid of immobile ommatidia cells deflecting and focusing the flow of non-ommatidia cells.
source: Flow in the MF is non-uniform owing to the lattice grid of immobile ommatidia cells deflecting and focusing the flow of non-ommatidia cells (Figure 7A and C).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figures 7A and C.

claim: The resulting fluid flow is significantly focused in the MF to create a periodic flow field.
source: The resulting fluid flow is significantly focused in the MF to create a periodic flow field.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The templating mechanism is mechanochemical in origin; newly formed columns of differentiating ommatidia serve as a template to spatially focus cell flow that will move cells into position to form the next column of ommatidia with the opposing parity.
source: In this sense, the templating mechanism is mechanochemical in origin; newly formed columns of differentiating ommatidia serve as a template to spatially focus cell flow that will move cells into position to form the next column of ommatidia with the opposing parity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: BMP and Hedgehog signals induce cells entering the MF to express the proneural gene atonal.
source: BMP and Hedgehog signals induce cells entering the MF to express the proneural gene atonal.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and is based on prior literature.

claim: A dorsal-ventral stripe of cells in the MF express the proneural transcription factor Atonal.
source: A dorsal-ventral stripe of cells in the MF express this proneural transcription factor (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The mechanical mechanism would lead to regularly spaced clusters of Atonal-positive cells being left behind by the MF, while the other Atonal-positive cells would continue moving with the MF.
source: The mechanism we describe would lead to regularly spaced clusters of Atonal-positive cells being left behind by the MF, while the other Atonal-positive cells would continue moving with the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: A striped atonal prepattern would be resolved to a lattice pattern of atonal expression by tissue mechanics.
source: Thus, a striped atonal prepattern would be resolved to a lattice pattern of atonal expression by tissue mechanics.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Non R cells in the PTZ are experiencing maximal dilation.
source: Non R cells in the PTZ are experiencing maximal dilation.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Ommatidia in the PTZ abruptly change their mobility relative to other cells, going from immobility to ambient mobility.
source: Ommatidia in the PTZ abruptly change their mobility relative to other cells, going from immobility to ambient mobility.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Posterior to the PTZ, ommatidia begin their rotation, and presumably the release from immobility enables rotation to occur.
source: Posterior to the PTZ, ommatidia begin their rotation, and presumably the release from immobility enables rotation to occur.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The PTZ remains a fixed distance from the MF as it migrates across the disc.
source: An important point to emphasize is that the PTZ remains a fixed distance from the MF as it migrates across the disc.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The fixed distance of the PTZ from the MF is crucial to maintain a constant pressure gradient toward the MF such that periodic flows would generate an invariant triangular grid of ommatidia across the eye field.
source: This would be crucial to maintain a constant pressure gradient toward the MF such that periodic flows would generate an invariant triangular grid of ommatidia across the eye field.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The fixed distance of the PTZ from the MF ensures that the pattern of immobile ommatidia in columns one and two focuses cell flow into alternating periodic clusters within the MF as it moves.
source: The fixed distance also ensures that the pattern of immobile ommatidia in columns one and two focuses cell flow into alternating periodic clusters within the MF as it moves.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Loss of Scabrous leads to diminished cell dilation in the PTZ, diminished cell flow, and broken emergence of the ommatidia lattice at the MF.
source: We found that loss of Scabrous leads to diminished cell dilation in the PTZ, diminished cell flow, and broken emergence of the ommatidia lattice at the MF.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: The simplest model is that Scabrous directly regulates cell dilation and consequently cell flow and patterning.
source: We favor the simplest model in which Scabrous directly regulates cell dilation and consequently cell flow and patterning.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as the authors' preferred model.

claim: This model fits with all previously published genetic data on Scabrous' role in eye development.
source: Note that this model fits with all previously published genetic data on Scabrous' role in eye development.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: It was suggested that Scabrous acts as a ligand for the Notch receptor, but this suggestion was not substantiated in the eye.
source: It was suggested that Scabrous acts as a ligand for the Notch receptor (Powell et al., 2001), but this suggestion was not substantiated in the eye (Lee et al., 1996; Roignant and Treisman, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Powell et al., 2001, Lee et al., 1996, and Roignant and Treisman, 2009.

claim: Scabrous mutants have a small but significant phenotype in which their ommatidia over-rotate.
source: Interestingly, scabrous mutants have a small but significant phenotype in which their ommatidia over-rotate (Chou and Chien, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chou and Chien, 2002.

claim: Null scabrous mutants had variable and partial effects on dilation and flow that correlated with their effects on ommatidia spacing.
source: We found that null scabrous mutants had variable and partial effects on dilation and flow that correlated with their effects on ommatidia spacing.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion.

claim: Variability in spacing phenotypes for the null scabrous mutant had been previously noted.
source: Variability in spacing phenotypes for the null scabrous mutant had been previously noted (Baker and Zitron, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Baker and Zitron, 1995.

claim: There is another signal important for spacing that is induced by EGFR.
source: There is another signal important for spacing that is induced by EGFR (Chen and Chien, 1999; Spencer et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen and Chien, 1999 and Spencer et al., 1998.

claim: The EGFR signal must act in parallel to Scabrous for ordering the triangular grid pattern, since a scabrous EGFR double mutant has more severe spacing defects than either single mutant.
source: This signal must act in parallel to Scabrous for ordering the triangular grid pattern, since a scabrous EGFR double mutant has more severe spacing defects than either single mutant (Baonza et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Baonza et al., 2001.

claim: It is possible that EGFR signaling also contributes to the pressure and flow fields that were discovered.
source: Therefore, it is possible that EGFR signaling also contributes to the pressure and flow fields that we have discovered.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a possibility.
